topic: Strange borders countdown: Hans Island whisky war split in 2022, plus five more real borders
hook: Your bottle of whisky once started a border war, and in 2022 Canada and Denmark finally split an island in half.
title: The Whisky War Island and 5 Stranger Borders
description:
A countdown of six real borders that look like mistakes on the map: a Spanish town inside France, a piece of America you reach through Canada, a country inside another country, the Hans Island whisky war, Russia's cut-off Baltic region, and the tangled India-Bangladesh enclaves. Every border here is real, and the last one is in India.

#borders #geography #factsyoucantbelieve

scenes.narration: Your bottle of whisky once started a border war, and in 2022 Canada and Denmark finally split an island in half.
scenes.headline: The Whisky War

scenes.narration: By the end, you will have seen six borders that look like mistakes on the map, and every one of them is real.
scenes.headline: Six Real Borders

scenes.narration: The last one is in India, and it was so tangled that two countries had to swap land to fix it.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Indian

scenes.narration: The whisky island is number three, so stay for the story of the bottles.
scenes.headline: Number Three

scenes.narration: We count down from six to one, and each border is stranger than the one before.
scenes.headline: Countdown Starts

scenes.narration: Number six: a small Spanish town called Llívia sits completely inside France, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Spain Inside France

scenes.narration: Drive through the Pyrenees mountains and you will pass Spanish town signs while every field around you belongs to France.
scenes.headline: Spanish Signs, French Fields

scenes.narration: The reason is an old treaty from 1659, when Spain handed France a list of villages.
scenes.headline: A Treaty From 1659

scenes.narration: Llívia was officially a town, not a village, so it was never on the list, and it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: People there speak Spanish and Catalan, pay in euros, and vote in Spain, even though France surrounds the whole town.
scenes.headline: Spanish Life, French Land

scenes.narration: A short road over French land links it to Spain, and Europe's open borders mean nobody stops you.
scenes.headline: The Road Home

scenes.narration: Try this on your map app: search for Llívia and zoom out. You will see Spain floating inside France.
scenes.headline: Try It On Your Phone

scenes.narration: So one word in a 1659 treaty left a Spanish town trapped inside France, and it is still there.
scenes.headline: One Word Did It

scenes.narration: But a town is small. Next is a piece of America that you can only reach by driving through Canada.
scenes.headline: Next: America Via Canada

scenes.narration: Number five: Point Roberts, a small corner of Washington state in the USA that hangs off the bottom of Canada.
scenes.headline: A Piece Of America

scenes.narration: Open your map app near Vancouver and zoom in. You will see a tiny American shape hanging below Canada's coast.
scenes.headline: Zoom In Near Vancouver

scenes.narration: The border follows a straight line, the 49th parallel, and this little peninsula falls just south of it.
scenes.headline: The 49th Parallel

scenes.narration: So it belongs to America, but the only road out of it goes into Canada.
scenes.headline: Only Road Is Canadian

scenes.narration: To reach the rest of the USA by road, residents must cross into Canada, then cross back out again.
scenes.headline: In, Then Out

scenes.narration: That means passing through border control twice, just to drive to another American town.
scenes.headline: Two Border Checks
scenes.sub: Just to stay in the USA

scenes.narration: Many Canadians own holiday homes there, but they can only reach them by crossing the border too.
scenes.headline: Canadian Holiday Homes

scenes.narration: The people who live there still hold American passports, vote in American elections, and use American money.
scenes.headline: Fully American

scenes.narration: On a map it looks like a typo: a piece of one country cut off by the shape of another.
scenes.headline: A Typo On The Map

scenes.narration: A straight line trapped those people. The next country is trapped by another country on every single side.
scenes.headline: Trapped On All Sides

scenes.narration: Number four: Lesotho, a whole country with no coast and only one neighbour, and that neighbour wraps all the way around it.
scenes.headline: A Country Inside A Country

scenes.narration: Look at southern Africa on any map. Lesotho is a country-shaped hole inside South Africa.
scenes.headline: A Hole In South Africa

scenes.narration: It is one of only a few countries in the world that are completely surrounded by another.
scenes.headline: Only A Few Like It

scenes.narration: Even its lowest point is high: the whole country sits more than one thousand metres above sea level.
scenes.headline: All Of It Is High

scenes.narration: People call it the Kingdom in the Sky, and its border with South Africa runs along rivers and mountains.
scenes.headline: Kingdom In The Sky

scenes.narration: Many people there wear thick woollen blankets, because the mountains get cold and snow does fall.
scenes.headline: Blankets And Snow

scenes.narration: The capital, Maseru, sits so close to the border that you can see South Africa from the city.
scenes.headline: Capital On The Border

scenes.narration: At Maseru Bridge, a short bridge over the Caledon River is where you cross between the two countries.
scenes.headline: A Short Bridge

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts like these, subscribe, because we find more of them every day.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places

scenes.narration: Now the one that started this video: two countries, one tiny rock, and a war fought with bottles.
scenes.headline: Now: The Bottle War

scenes.narration: Number three: Hans Island, a bare rock in the freezing water between Canada and Greenland.
scenes.headline: Hans Island

scenes.narration: It is just over one square kilometre in size, with no trees, no people and no town.
scenes.headline: A Bare Rock

scenes.narration: It is named after Hans Hendrik, a Greenlandic Arctic traveller who helped early expeditions in the area.
scenes.headline: Named After Hans

scenes.narration: In 1973 Canada and Denmark drew their sea border, but they left this one rock undecided.
scenes.headline: One Rock Left Out

scenes.narration: Both said it was theirs. Greenland belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark, so Denmark claimed it too.
scenes.headline: Both Said Mine

scenes.narration: In 1984, Canadian soldiers landed, planted a flag, and left a bottle of Canadian whisky behind.
scenes.headline: Canada's Whisky

scenes.narration: Soon a Danish minister landed, planted a Danish flag, and left schnapps with a note saying welcome to the Danish island.
scenes.headline: Denmark's Reply

scenes.narration: For years, visitors kept swapping flags and bottles. People called it the Whisky War, and nobody ever fired a shot.
scenes.headline: No Shots Fired

scenes.narration: Both sides stayed friendly the whole time. Canada and Denmark are close partners, so it was always a polite fight.
scenes.headline: A Polite Fight

scenes.narration: Getting there means crossing icy water, so the people who visited were mostly soldiers, officials and scientists.
scenes.headline: Hard To Reach

scenes.narration: Finally, on 14 June 2022, both countries agreed to share the rock and split it down the middle.
scenes.headline: Split In 2022

scenes.narration: The new border on the island is just over a kilometre long, and follows a natural ridge in the rock.
scenes.headline: A Border On A Ridge

scenes.narration: That gave Canada a second land border, and its first one with a European country.
scenes.headline: Canada's New Border

scenes.narration: Two countries chose friendship over a fight, and ended a war that ran for almost forty years.
scenes.headline: Ended After 38 Years

scenes.narration: Next is a Russian region on the Baltic Sea that no road from Russia can reach without crossing other countries.
scenes.headline: Next: Cut-Off Russia

scenes.narration: Number two: Kaliningrad, a Russian region that is not connected to the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: Russia's Cut-Off Region

scenes.narration: Poland sits on one side of it and Lithuania on the other, and both are in the European Union.
scenes.headline: Surrounded By The EU

scenes.narration: So Russian land sits on the European map like a missing puzzle piece, far from Russia's main territory.
scenes.headline: A Missing Piece

scenes.narration: The area used to be German, a city called Königsberg, until it was handed to the Soviet Union after World War Two.
scenes.headline: Once Königsberg

scenes.narration: The famous philosopher Immanuel Kant lived his whole life in that city, when it was still called Königsberg.
scenes.headline: Kant Lived Here

scenes.narration: Most Germans left or were forced out, Russians moved in, and the city got a new name.
scenes.headline: A New People, New Name

scenes.narration: In 1946 it was named Kaliningrad, after a Soviet leader called Mikhail Kalinin.
scenes.headline: Named For Kalinin

scenes.narration: Today, to get there by land, Russian citizens must pass through other countries, because no direct route exists.
scenes.headline: No Direct Route

scenes.narration: On a map it looks like a mistake, yet around a million people live there.
scenes.headline: A Million People

scenes.narration: But the strangest border of all is right here in India, and it was only fixed in 2015.
scenes.headline: Now, India's Turn

scenes.narration: Number one: the Cooch Behar enclaves on the India and Bangladesh border, often called the strangest border on Earth.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest Border

scenes.narration: Our own backyard hides it, in north Bengal, in the district of Cooch Behar, right by the Bangladesh border.
scenes.headline: North Bengal

scenes.narration: More than a hundred and fifty tiny islands of land, each belonging to one country but sitting inside the other.
scenes.headline: Islands Of Land

scenes.narration: In total, 111 Indian pieces of land sat inside Bangladesh, and 51 Bangladeshi pieces sat inside India.
scenes.headline: 111 And 51

scenes.narration: Some were just a few farm fields. People could walk out of their front door and into another country.
scenes.headline: A Few Farm Fields

scenes.narration: The tangle goes back centuries to local rulers whose lands were mixed together, long before India and Bangladesh existed.
scenes.headline: Centuries Old

scenes.narration: When Britain divided India in 1947, the land stayed mixed, and the new border had to run around every single piece.
scenes.headline: Partition, 1947

scenes.narration: Villagers often struggled to get roads, schools, hospitals or electricity, because neither government could easily reach them.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Help

scenes.narration: And it gets worse. One plot, called Dahala Khagrabari, was Indian land inside Bangladeshi land inside Indian land inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: That is four layers of countries in one small farm field, the only one of its kind in the world.
scenes.headline: Four Layers

scenes.narration: Then on the night of 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped the land.
scenes.headline: Midnight Swap

scenes.narration: Many residents celebrated that night, as the flags of their new country went up over their villages.
scenes.headline: Flags Go Up

scenes.narration: People living there were allowed to choose which country they wanted to belong to.
scenes.headline: People Chose

scenes.narration: Thousands of people changed their country overnight without moving an inch from their own homes.
scenes.headline: New Country, Same Home

scenes.narration: It took a treaty from 1974 and many years of delay, but the tangle was finally cleared.
scenes.headline: Cleared After 41 Years

scenes.narration: And that is how a border war once fought with bottles of whisky became one of the calmest endings on any map.
scenes.headline: From Bottles To Peace

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: the country that has no border at its own front door.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow
scenes.sub: A front door with no border
